- **Green stems** remaining while pods are mature/dried brown (papery)
- No leaves present (defoliated)
- Some dark discoloration at nodes
- Classic "green stem persisting at maturity" appearance

Top candidates: **Green_stem_disorder**, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (green stem symptom), Tobacco_Streak_Virus

Let me view reference images to confirm.
The Green_stem_disorder reference is an excellent match — green stems with mature dried pods and no leaves. Let me view more references to meet the requirement.

All 12 reference images reviewed. The diagnosis is clear.

**Analysis:**
- Test image shows **green stems persisting** at full maturity while pods are completely dried/brown and papery
- Plants are fully defoliated (leaves dropped)
- Surrounding field material is dry/senesced
- Green_stem_disorder reference images are a near-perfect visual match — identical presentation of green stems with mature dried pods and no leaves

All other candidates were eliminated:
- Leaf disease classes (Frogeye, Septoria, SDS, etc.) — require leaf lesions, not present
- Stem rot diseases (BSR, Phytophthora) — require discolored stems, not green
- Virus diseases (BPMV, SDMV) — primarily show leaf mottling/distortion
- White_Mold, Anthracnose, Diaporthe — show fungal structures on stems/pods
